title: Stress rises when cellular memory fails to predict the future

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Stress rises when cellular memory fails to predict the future

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, stress increases concurrently with a fall in local active information storage of cell states, so evolution used the stress system as a communication channel activated when memory of past events does not predict the future, matching the definition of stressors as unpredictable or uncontrollable stimuli.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In our scheme, evolution used the stress system as a communication system that was activated when memory of past events was not effective for predicting the future.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Computational results › Information-theoretic analysis of the dynamics of the anatomical homeostasis”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public code makes the correlation and its robustness readily testable. The stronger functional interpretation requires counterfactual interventions not supplied by an observational information-storage analysis, though those interventions may be implementable in the model.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Regenerate cell-state and stress trajectories, compute local active information storage, and test whether stress rises when predictive storage falls. Intervene on prediction errors while holding energy and state constant to distinguish a prediction-failure channel from a correlated stress signal.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Concurrent changes do not establish that failed prediction activates stress.

The psychological analogy admits competing operationalizations.

The model's stress variable is defined by construction.

data adequacy: 0.8
analysis feasibility: 0.88
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Stress and active information storage are defined quantitatively, so their timing can be recomputed from logged runs of the public model. The repository does not contain the analyzed trajectories, and the evolutionary claim that stress was recruited as a channel for failed prediction is an interpretation of a correlation. Re-evolution would speak to whether the correlation is typical.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Plot mean local active information storage of cell state against stress in the same runs, with stress discretized in chunks of 10. Stress rising while active information storage of the white and red stripes falls, then the reverse as stress falls, would confirm the reported concurrence; stress spikes with flat or rising storage would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The blue stripe has zero active information storage because those cells never change state, so the tissue average is structurally biased.

The reported concurrence is from a representative run, and the winner network is not deposited.
